newsitem.title: INDIA: India rice traders look to Sri Lanka, Ethiopia.
newsitem.headline: India rice traders look to Sri Lanka, Ethiopia.

text.p: Indian rice traders are negotiating export deals with Sri Lanka, Ethiopia and Bangladesh, exporters said on Thursday.
"Demand is building up from these countries," Prem Garg, managing director of Sri Lal Mahal Overseas Ltd, told Reuters.
Traders said Indian exporters have already signed contracts to export nearly 100,000 tonnes of rice to Sri Lanka and 25,000 tonnes to Ethiopia.
"We are also expecting a substantial amount of rice exports to Bangladesh," said an official at a leading Delhi foodgrains export firm, who asked not to be identified.
Traders said Indian five percent broken non-Basmati rice was quoted at $300 a tonne F.O.B, 10 percent grade at $285 a tonne, 15 percent at $255 a tonne, and 25 percent at $235-$240 a tonne.
Traders said the Indian rice harvest was in full flow with 40 percent of the harvest already completed. The winter rice output is expected to be nearly two million tonnes more than the previous year.
"Rice arrivals in the markets has increased to nearly 35,000 tonnes per day from 20,000 tonnes last week," Garg said.
The agriculture ministry on Monday said India's 1996/97 (July-June) winter rice output was estimated at 71.27 million tonnes, up from 69.69 million tonnes in the previous season.
India harvests two rice crops, getting the bulk of its annual output from the winter crop. Sowing for the winter crop begins in July and the harvest starts from October.
